title: Obama-footage ad praising Haley Stevens' auto-rescue work
issue_or_message: Links Stevens to Barack Obama and to the 2008-2009 auto rescue
main_visual_elements: Archival footage of Barack Obama praising Stevens' work as chief of staff of the Auto Rescue Task Force
candidate_appearance: Haley Stevens is the subject; Obama appears in archive footage. El-Sayed does not appear.
main_claims: Stevens helped save the auto industry alongside Obama
fact_check: CNN reported Obama had not endorsed in the primary; Bridge Michigan fact-checked the ad's implication (SRC-0032, SRC-0014)
notes: Spent about $5 million and aired nearly 4,000 times, the most-run political ad in Michigan over the prior year per AdImpact. candidate_id is the Democratic nominee because the ad ran in the Democratic primary; it was not authorised by his campaign. Sponsor spent to support Stevens and oppose El-Sayed.

title: Direct-mail piece accusing El-Sayed of antisemitism
main_claims: El-Sayed is antisemitic because of his 'Hurt people hurt people' remark after the Temple Israel attack
fact_check: El-Sayed apologised for the remark; the mailer's characterisation is contested (SRC-0002)
notes: $94,620 on direct mail targeted at 130,000 Jewish voters, per NBC News as cited by The American Prospect. UDP began spending less than 24 hours after Rogers said at the Oct 8 debate that he would accept AIPAC help. This is an independent expenditure, not a candidate-committee ad.

title: Ad linking U.S. military aid to Israel with the cost-of-living crisis
main_claims: U.S. aid to Israel is connected to household cost pressures
fact_check: Stevens called the ad antisemitic and demanded El-Sayed condemn it; El-Sayed said he was unaffiliated with it (SRC-0001)
notes: The ad is described in the race article as released in the week before Stevens' endorsement. The sponsoring group's name was not retrievable, so the sponsor field describes it functionally rather than naming it.

title: Primary television flight against El-Sayed
main_claims: Attack ads on El-Sayed and ads defending Stevens' record
notes: Axios reported a 12-to-1 spending advantage for Stevens at that point in the primary; no individual spot was retrieved, so the row records the flight rather than a single advertisement.
